255.t: David Jones as a musician and the Lutcher picture
255.s: Jones played tenor and drums and other instruments, appeared in a band photo with Kid Ory, and worked at a music store when Lee Collins was there.
255.q: Well, according to his record, he could play several instruments. His place was a drum. Now, we have a picture of him from Lutcher, from Mr. Joseph. Yeah, he got one out at the shop. Of him, Aura, Kid Aura, and Professor David Jones, and Professor Holmes. They had a band of their own way back. And…

873.t: Players who trained with Lawrence and left: Halls, Arsenault, French brothers
873.s: Lawrence names former band members and their instruments, including Clarence Hall, Herbert Trish, Roland Arsenault, Leroy, the French brothers, Fredo, Marzell and Lawrence Dewey.
873.q: And Leroy played the tenor sax. And my boy June, he played, Marshall Lawrence, he played saxophone. And this French boy, I forget it. What relation is he to Morris? His brother. That's his brother.

818.t: Salvaggio band personnel: Philip Salvaggio, Perkins, DeShari, Pudra
818.s: Joe Salvaggio played piano, brother Philip led on alto and clarinet; tenor men George Perkins and Jack DeShari, and bass horn John Pudra.
818.q: He's a very fine piano player. Very fine pianist. He still plays. He's around still playing. His brother played lead alto sax and clarinet. I don't know if the brothers playing sax and clarinet any more, but Joe, the leader of the group, was a very fine musician.

54.s: Barnes played tenor sax; the interviewers run through his sidemen, and McAllister met most but knew none locally.
54.q: Mostly tenor. Every time I seen him, he was playing sax.

659.s: He names tenor players King Curtis, Sam Taylor, David Newman and guitarists Mickey Baker, Eric Gale and others, and contrasts rhythm sections with horn players who play what is on the page.
659.q: King Curtis was the tenor sax soloist. Sam “the Man” Taylor, David Newman, Marshall Royal. I mean all these guys were all legends to me. And guitar players was Mickey

227.s: They name the saxophone section of Shaw's band, with Herbie Steward, Al Cohn, Socolow, Zoot Sims and Danny Bank.
227.ch: Count Basie, Artie Shaw and the soprano experiments
227.q: Zoot, yeah that’s right! That is the best saxophone section probably that Danny Bank ever played in. Herbie was playing lead alto, he turned out to be a wonderful alto player.

80.t: Doc Hyder's band personnel and the sax player who never bought a reed
80.s: A 12-13 piece band including Bernard Archer, Lincoln Mills, Wilkins, Puny and Watkins, a brilliant reed player who never bought a reed.
80.ch: New York, Henderson and Charlie Johnson
80.q: Aw, he had what, 12 or 13 pieces then, had a big band, you know. Well I always thought we had three or four brass, and same with saxes, and you know, and the rhythm, and whatnot. And had some good musicians, too.

26.t: Rudy Jackson, Harry Carney and Nelson Kincaid
26.s: Greer recalls early saxophonists and a trumpeter.
26.q: Oh, he played saxophone. Rudy Jackson, Brother Rudy, yeah. Rudy Jackson. He just played -- Rudy Jackson played with us -- let me see, he played with us at Salem Willows. But Rudy played with the band before Carny.

70.t: Chick Webb's trumpet and reed sections
70.s: Jackson lists Webb's best band with Vance, Stark and Jordan and a sax section of Jefferson, Carver, Elmer Williams and Pete Clark.
70.ch: Musicians of the era: players, drummers, bassists, pianists
70.q: A very good band he had. He had a beautiful band when he had Dick Vance and Bobby Stark and he had Taft Jordan.

232.t: Sidemen who passed through the band: Geesil Minerve and Harold Bruce
232.s: Fields lists players who went on to big bands, such as Geesil Minerve and Harold Bruce.
232.ch: Touring in the bus years and Jim Crow in the South
232.q: Yes, Harold Bruce. I've had some of the greats, and they always said--you know, I had that reputation about music, well, the guys always knew--I'll tell you another band that used to work on some, was Nat.

29.t: Charlie Jones, saxophonist with Lionel and Les Hite
29.s: Howard says Charlie Jones played with Lionel and later with Les Hite.
29.ch: Reel 2: Los Angeles musicians, the Apex and Cotton Club
29.q: He was a good saxophone player, and he played with -- in the band.
